q: Which is the largest of the world's oceans?
note: The Pacific covers more of the globe than all the world's dry land put together.

q: Which river flows the length of Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean?
note: Ancient Egypt depended on the Nile's yearly flood, which the Aswan High Dam has held back since the 1960s.

q: Which river runs through Paris?
note: The Seine empties into the English Channel at the port of Le Havre.

q: Which is the largest of the five Great Lakes?
note: Superior holds more water than the other four Great Lakes combined.

q: Which river forms the border between Texas and Mexico?
note: On the Mexican side the same river is called the Rio Bravo.

q: Which river flows through London?
note: The Thames is tidal through London and runs east into the North Sea.

q: Which is the largest lake in the world by surface area?
note: Despite the name it is a landlocked lake, bordered by Russia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean to which sea?
note: The strait is only about eight miles across at its narrowest point.

q: Which river flows through Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade?
note: The Danube touches ten countries on its way to the Black Sea, more than any other river.

q: Which lake, bordered by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya, is the largest in Africa?
note: The White Nile begins at its northern shore in Uganda.

q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
note: This Siberian lake holds roughly a fifth of all the unfrozen fresh surface water on Earth.

q: Which sacred Indian river flows past Varanasi and empties into the Bay of Bengal?
note: The Ganges begins as meltwater in the Himalayas before crossing the plains of northern India.

q: Which body of water between Israel and Jordan sits at the lowest land elevation on Earth?
note: Its shore lies more than 1,300 feet below sea level, and the water is salty enough to float a swimmer.

q: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
note: It is the only ocean named after a country.

q: Which major river flows north through Germany and the Netherlands into the North Sea?
note: The Rhine marked the frontier of the Roman Empire and has been a trade artery ever since.

q: What is the name of the deepest known trench in the world's oceans?
note: Its deepest point, the Challenger Deep, lies nearly 36,000 feet down in the western Pacific near Guam.

q: Which sea has no coastline at all, its edges defined instead by ocean currents?
note: It sits in the North Atlantic, ringed by four currents, and is named for the sargassum seaweed that drifts there.

q: Which is the longest river in Asia?
note: The Three Gorges Dam spans it, and the river runs entirely within China.

q: Which is the longest river in Europe?
note: The Volga flows entirely inside Russia and drains into the Caspian Sea rather than any ocean.

q: Which African lake is the longest freshwater lake in the world?
note: It stretches roughly 400 miles along the Great Rift Valley and is the second deepest lake on Earth.
